canonical_name: Jordan-Holder uniqueness of group composition factors
literal_source_claim_zh: 群的合成列在同构意义下唯一
literal_source_claim_en: A group's composition series is unique up to isomorphism.
source_attribution: Camille Jordan and Otto Holder, 1889 (catalog metadata only; not a source citation)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a source-selected finite group, or more generally a group admitting finite composition series, any two composition series have equal finite length and their simple successive quotient groups are isomorphic after a permutation of factors.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not define a composition series, fix finite-group versus conditional finite-length scope, choose chain orientation and endpoints, state successor normality and quotient simplicity, decide whether existence is included, or define uniqueness as a permutation matching quotient groups. Milne v4.01 is a strong modern source lead but is uncited and unreviewed. Pinned mathlib proves only the abstract JordanHolderLattice theorem and explicitly lacks the subgroup realization. Selecting an exact proposition now would invent or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must select a finite group G or an arbitrary group supplied with finite composition series, then freeze the carrier universe, Group and finiteness interfaces, proof-carrying subnormal chain representation, endpoints, quotient construction, and normality witnesses.
conclusion: Open: exact equal-length and factor-permutation conclusion, including the quotient group isomorphism type and whether existence is part of the root, is not selected.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no canonical proposition is frozen; the trivial group, simple groups, zero- and one-factor series, identical series, repeated isomorphic factors, infinite finite-length groups, chain orientation, and invalid repeated or nonsimple steps remain explicit statement decisions.
